messages.enterEscape: The lights will dim and the doors will seal behind you. Everything you studied in the gallery will help you find your way out. Step inside?
messages.doorLocked: The lock is cold and patient. Solve each painting's puzzle to uncover the digits of the code.
messages.doorUnlocked: The door stands open. The corridor remembers you fondly.
messages.exitClosed: The exit stays closed during gallery hours. Study the paintings. You will need what they teach you.
messages.escaped: The door swings wide and the evening air feels wonderful. The corridor will remember what you learned.
messages.doorNudge: The lock does not stir. Check the digits and their order.

ui.sessionResumed: Your escape room session was resumed.

artworks.title: The Patient Watcher
artworks.curatorNote: Placeholder note: notice how the sitter's gaze seems to follow you down the hall.
artworks.lesson: Placeholder lesson: a keyboard has many keys, yet it unlocks no door. Riddles often describe a thing by what it has and what it lacks.

puzzle.prompt: I have keys but no locks. What am I?
puzzle.hint: You are probably touching one right now.
puzzle.nudge: Think about what sits under your hands as you type.
puzzle.explanation: A keyboard has keys, yet nothing for them to unlock.

artworks.title: Lantern at Low Tide
artworks.curatorNote: Placeholder note: the painter used a single lantern to light the whole shoreline.
artworks.lesson: Placeholder lesson: the Moon's pull on the ocean causes tides, so the water rises and falls twice a day.

puzzle.prompt: What mainly causes the ocean tides?
puzzle.hint: It is the bright thing that watches the shore at night.
puzzle.nudge: Look up at the night sky for your answer.
puzzle.explanation: The Moon's gravity pulls on the ocean and raises the tides.

artworks.title: The Quiet Staircase
artworks.curatorNote: Placeholder note: each step is drawn a little darker than the last.
artworks.lesson: Placeholder lesson: an echo is sound that bounces off a surface and returns to your ears.

puzzle.prompt: I speak without a mouth and answer only when you call. What am I?
puzzle.hint: Try calling out in an empty stairwell.
puzzle.nudge: Think of a sound that comes back to you.
puzzle.explanation: An echo is your own sound reflected back from a surface.

artworks.title: The Cartographer's Window
artworks.curatorNote: Placeholder note: the mapmaker painted the sunrise through his own window, always on the same side.
artworks.lesson: Placeholder lesson: the Sun rises in the east and sets in the west, because Earth turns toward the east.

puzzle.prompt: In which direction does the Sun rise?
puzzle.hint: Mapmakers mark it on the right-hand side of a standard map.
puzzle.nudge: Face the morning light and name the direction.
puzzle.explanation: Earth turns toward the east, so the Sun appears to rise there.

artworks.title: The Clock Without Hands
artworks.curatorNote: Placeholder note: the face is complete, yet the hands were never painted.
artworks.lesson: Placeholder lesson: a clock has hands that point to the hour and minute, though it cannot clap or wave.

puzzle.prompt: I have hands but cannot clap. What am I?
puzzle.hint: You may glance at one on the wall before class.
puzzle.nudge: Think of something that tells you the time.
puzzle.explanation: A clock has hands that point to the time, but they cannot clap.

artworks.title: The Last Candle
artworks.curatorNote: Placeholder note: a single candle is the only light in an otherwise empty hall.
artworks.lesson: Placeholder lesson: a flame needs oxygen to keep burning, so a candle goes out when the air is cut off.

puzzle.prompt: What does a flame need to keep burning?
puzzle.hint: It is the part of the air that you breathe in.
puzzle.nudge: A jar placed over a candle takes this away.
puzzle.explanation: Fire needs oxygen, so a flame goes out when the oxygen runs low.
